extraction.name: MATH
extraction.description: A dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems with full step-by-step solutions written in LaTeX and natural language, designed to measure mathematical problem-solving ability in machine learning models across seven subjects and five difficulty levels.
extraction.creator: Dan Hendrycks, Collin Burns, Saurav Kadavath, Akul Arora, Steven Basart, Eric Tang, Dawn Song, Jacob Steinhardt
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MATH problems were collected from high school mathematics competitions including the AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, and more, spanning decades, many collected from aops.com/community/c3158_usa_contests. The auxiliary pretraining dataset AMPS was collected from Khan Academy (github.com/Khan/khan-exercises/) and generated via 100 Mathematica scripts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: High school math competitions (AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, etc.) via AoPS, Khan Academy exercises, and Mathematica scripts.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Problems and solutions were formatted in LaTeX and Asymptote vector graphics language. Final boxed answers follow strict normalization rules: probabilities as simplified fractions, specific fraction encodings, variable expressions in alphabetical order, polynomials in decreasing degree order, factorized polynomial permutations permitted, and delimiters handled with \boxed{}.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Separated into 7,500 training and 5,000 test problems, categorized into seven subjects and difficulty levels 1 to 5.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Difficulty levels were tagged from 1 to 5 following AoPS. Final answers were formatted and delimited using \boxed{} to enable automatic exact-match evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: High performance on the dataset could have ramifications for cheating on homework. The authors explicitly state they do not intend for the dataset to train models that help students cheat on mathematics exams.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Model accuracy remains low (3.0% to 6.9%), and scaling model size yields slow progress. Language models struggle to use their own generated step-by-step solutions without derailment and exhibit overconfidence (AUROC of 68.8% for error detection).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking mathematical problem-solving ability, training models to generate answer derivations and step-by-step explanations, fine-tuning, and forecasting reasoning capabilities. Not intended for training models to help students cheat on math exams.
